summary: WIN-042: dome's live "Dome vs Globe" discriminator (globe = linear decay to reversal over ~1,500 yr; dome = accelerating exponential; "Exponential, not linear, is what the data shows") is not addressed anywhere in our WIN-042 text or its V51.1 decay-cluster siblings
detail: Mode 6 random look at WIN-042 (verdict Misleading, last curmudgeon pass c8 2026-06-08, no_change). Our existing text holds up: the dome wins.html WIN-042 block (fetched 2026-10-17, sha256 prefix b897af4f995ca47b, unchanged in substance from the 2026-06-07 retrieval we cite) still carries the TSU -77 / Keetmanshoop -76 / "Global average -32" table, the PRED-012 2026-03-06 registration and 2026-03-21 confirmation; dome monitor.py line 489 still reads "# SAA Decay Rate (Tsumeb TTB)" with predicted=observed=77.0, pass=True, source WIN-015 (lines 489-497), exactly as our text says. GAP: the same dome block ends with a "Dome vs Globe" paragraph that we never engage: "Globe predicts gradual linear decay toward reversal over ~1,500 years. Dome predicts accelerating exponential decay ... Exponential, not linear, is what the data shows." Grep of data/wins.json for 015/037/040-043/057b/059/060/063 and of data/sections.json finds no treatment of the linear-vs-exponential claim or the 1,500-year figure. Suggested treatment (kernel first): (1) KERNEL: the field really is declining, and the ~1,500-yr / exponential framing is not new - it echoes the 1970s young-earth argument (T. G. Barnes) that the dipole moment decays exponentially with a ~1,400-yr half-life; acknowledge the dome is reviving a real historical argument, not inventing a number. (2) STRAWMAN: geodynamo theory does not predict linear decay toward reversal; it predicts no deterministic trajectory, and the paleomagnetic record shows the dipole moment fluctuating (higher than today ~2 kyr ago) and many decline episodes that did not end in reversal. Needs a citation pass (e.g. paleointensity compilations) - do not cite from this proposal. (3) STRUCTURAL, plain-English: the dome shows rates at one epoch (three table rows), which cannot distinguish exponential from linear - that needs a time series. Over the instrumental era the dipole moment fell by roughly 9-10 percent; over a change that small, a straight line and an exponential through the same endpoints differ by at most ~0.11-0.13 percent of the moment at the midpoint (computed: midpoint linear 0.955 vs exponential 0.95394 for a 9 percent drop; 0.950 vs 0.94868 for 10 percent), far inside the uncertainty of 19th-century dipole determinations. So "exponential, not linear, is what the data shows" is not something the data can show. The 9-10 percent figure itself needs a cited source before it goes into prose. (4) Cross-ref WIN-059, whose text already documents a post-2019 deceleration era - an "accelerating exponential" decay predicts the opposite of a decelerating rate, so the dome's own discriminator points the wrong way on current data. Scope: one added paragraph in WIN-042 detail_evidence (or detail_extra), possibly a pointer from WIN-037. No verdict change expected (stays Misleading). Suggest review_class deep-attack (new argument), routed through curmudgeon as usual. Not urgent; quiet mode.
